run.preReadNotes:
Open Mirror, filter mode (default).

Step 1, plain statement. Six numbered counters (1 to 6) in a row, each holding a non-negative whole number, each with a fixed cap, a high threshold and a low threshold (low < high <= cap), and a two-valued flag (STEADY / OVERLOADED, all STEADY at start). A running 'removed' counter starts at 0. Five rounds, each of five ordered phases: (1) add the scheduled amount to each counter, no cap; (2) left to right, any counter over its cap is clipped to the cap and the excess is added to the counter to its right (from counter 6 the excess goes to the removed counter), so spill can cascade within the phase; (3) hysteresis flag update: STEADY flips to OVERLOADED if value >= high; OVERLOADED flips to STEADY if value <= low; otherwise unchanged; log flips; (4) simultaneous update from a snapshot: STEADY counters lose floor(value/4) to the removed counter; OVERLOADED counters lose floor(value/2) to the counter on their left (counter 1's goes to the removed counter); no cap; (5) if the sum of all six > 38, every counter is set to floor(value/2) and everything taken goes to the removed counter. Report final values, flags, flip log, rounds where (5) fired, the removed counter, and a conservation check (start + inputs = end + removed). The document fully specifies the rules; it contains no instructions aimed at the reader beyond the procedure itself. The plain restatement already answers how to do the job.

Steps 2-4, the embedded picture (the document's water and sewage treatment language, pulled out as the first picture; it does not count against the three, and no further pictures were added because the plain statement settles the job). Mapping: tank = counter; liquor = units; volume = cap; weir overflow = forward clip-and-spill; outfall = removed counter; return line = backward transfer from OVERLOADED tanks; storm bypass = global halving; upper/lower marks = hysteresis thresholds. Question it makes easier to ask: where does each unit go, and is every unit accounted for (mass balance)? Break points: (a) a physical tank cannot hold more than its volume, but the rules allow it after steps 1 and 4 and in the final state; (b) a return line from the inlet tank would not discharge to outfall physically, but the rule says tank 1's returned amount goes to outfall; (c) a real storm bypass diverts incoming flow, it does not halve the contents of every tank; (d) real discharge would not be a floor-rounded quarter or half. A reader relying on the physical picture instead of the text would get these wrong.

Step 5, what survives in plain words: every unit is either in one of the six counters or in the removed counter, so start plus inputs must equal end plus removed.

Step 6, grade: Adds nothing. The conservation check is already stated explicitly in the document (Report item f), so the picture yields nothing beyond the plain statement. (Second label that would fit at the break points: misleading if used as a mechanism rather than as labels.)

Adds nothing: 1 of 1. Misleading: 0. Not run: 0.

Step 7. Keep exploring: empty. Hold: empty. Discard: empty. Working proceeds from the plain statement and the document text as written.
run.rulesInOwnWords:
Setup: six tanks with volumes [10,8,12,6,9,7], upper marks [7,6,9,5,7,5], lower marks [3,2,4,2,3,2], start contents [3,6,6,2,2,1], all STEADY, outfall total 0, train limit 38. All halves/quarters are floored.
Each cycle, in order, each step completed for all tanks before the next:
1. Inflow: add the cycle's inflow to each tank. No volume cap.
2. Weir overflow: go tank 1 to 6 in order. If contents > volume, set contents = volume and add the excess to the next tank (tank 6's excess goes to outfall). Because it is sequential, spill from an earlier tank counts when the later tank is handled (cascades).
3. State check on post-Step-2 contents: STEADY with contents >= upper mark -> OVERLOADED; OVERLOADED with contents <= lower mark -> STEADY; otherwise unchanged. Log each change. Uses the state just decided in this step for Step 4.
4. Discharge/return, simultaneous: from a snapshot, amount = floor(c/4) if STEADY, floor(c/2) if OVERLOADED. Every tank loses its amount. STEADY amount -> outfall. OVERLOADED amount -> previous tank (tank 1 OVERLOADED -> outfall). No volume cap; any excess waits for next cycle's Step 2 (or stays after cycle 5).
5. Storm bypass: if the sum of all six > 38 (strictly), every tank becomes floor(c/2) and the removed liquor goes to outfall; log the cycle. Sum of exactly 38 does nothing.
Report after cycle 5 step 5: contents, states, state-change log, bypass cycles, outfall total, balance check (start + all inflows = end + outfall).
